before.title: 8-Speed DCT Overheating Under Load / Towing
before.description: The 8-speed wet dual-clutch transmission (DCT) on the 2.5L turbo Santa Cruz can overheat when towing near its 5,000 lb capacity or during spirited driving in warm weather. The transmission overheating warning forces the vehicle into limp mode. The DCT cooling system is undersized for heavy-duty use.
before.solution: Avoid towing above 4,000 lbs in hot weather. Use tow/haul mode which adjusts shift patterns to reduce heat. An aftermarket transmission cooler ($200-400 installed) significantly helps. If overheating occurs, pull over and let the transmission cool for 15-20 minutes. Hyundai software update improves thermal management.
symptoms: Vehicle enters limp mode while towing
Harsh shifts when transmission is hot

citations.title: Hyundai TSB 22-AT-008 - DCT Thermal Management Update

communityRecommendations.content: Mishimoto universal transmission cooler provides excellent additional cooling capacity
Always use Tow/Haul mode when towing - it prevents the transmission from hunting gears and reduces heat buildup
Do not ignore the transmission overheat warning - continued driving can cause permanent clutch damage costing $3,000+

before.title: 12V Battery Parasitic Drain and Premature Failure
before.description: Santa Cruz owners report the 12V battery going dead after the vehicle sits only a few days, attributed to parasitic draw from the Bluelink telematics modem and constant key-fob pinging. Owners receive Bluelink low-battery alerts on nearly-new trucks, and some have had batteries discharge and require replacement under warranty at low mileage. This overlaps a broader Hyundai Bluelink standby-draw issue.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform a parasitic-draw test and replace a weak battery under warranty. Mitigate by using a battery maintainer when parked, avoiding the accessory/power-on setting, locking the vehicle to stop fob pinging, and changing the Bluelink password; Hyundai limited Bluelink server traffic (about 20 transactions/day) to reduce standby draw.
symptoms: Dead or weak 12V battery after sitting a few days

before.title: Forward Collision Avoidance Phantom / Unexpected Braking (Recall 26V316)
before.description: On 2025-2026 Santa Cruz (and Tucson) models, front-camera software makes the Forward Collision Avoidance system overly sensitive to forward object proximity, causing it to apply automatic braking earlier than the driver expects. This phantom braking can trigger sudden hard stops with no real hazard present, raising the risk of being rear-ended. Hyundai received 376 front-camera reports including four crashes and four injuries.
before.solution: Recall 26V316 (Hyundai campaign 302) remedy: dealers update the front-camera software free of charge to reduce FCA sensitivity. Owner notifications mailed beginning mid-July 2026. Verify by VIN at nhtsa.gov.
symptoms: Sudden automatic emergency braking with no obstacle present
Forward collision warning alerts without cause

citations.title: NHTSA Part 573 Safety Recall Report 26V316
Hyundai Recalls the Santa Cruz and Tucson Due to Brake Concerns (Consumer Reports)

proposal.title: Forward Collision Avoidance Phantom / Unexpected Braking (Recall 26V316)
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 26V-316 (Hyundai recall 302) covers certain model-year 2025-2026 Santa Cruz vehicles. Front-camera software can cause the Forward Collision Avoidance system to exhibit increased sensitivity to forward-object proximity in certain driving scenarios. The system may engage earlier than the driver expects and cause sudden braking, increasing the risk of a rear-end crash from a closely following vehicle.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for NHTSA recall 26V-316. Hyundai dealers update the front-camera software free of charge. The remedy software is tuned to better align activation timing and distance to the leading vehicle with operator expectations.
symptoms: Unexpected early Forward Collision Avoidance engagement

before.title: Roof Side Molding Detachment While Driving (Recall 23V-038)
before.description: Certain 2022-2023 Santa Cruz vehicles have roof side moldings with insufficient retention between the roof flange and mounting clips (caused by inconsistent paint-sealer application). The molding can loosen and detach during operation, becoming a road hazard for following vehicles and increasing crash risk. Roughly 16,104 Santa Cruz and Tucson units were affected.
before.solution: Recall 23V-038 remedy: dealers inspect and either re-secure or replace the roof moldings free of charge. Owner notification letters were mailed March 30, 2023; verify by VIN at nhtsa.gov.
symptoms: Lifting or flapping roof trim at highway speed
Visible gap between roof molding and body

before.title: Sunroof Drain Clogging Causing Interior Water Leaks
before.description: Santa Cruz owners report water leaking into the cabin, frequently onto the front passenger floorboard, traced to clogged, crimped, or disconnected sunroof drain hoses. In several documented cases dealers found multiple drain slots blocked or a factory drain hole that was never fully punched, so water backs up out of the sunroof pan and into the interior.
before.solution: Clear and re-route the sunroof drain hoses; verify all drain slots are open and the factory drain holes are fully formed. Owners report success vacuuming debris and blowing compressed air through the drains; dealers should inspect for crimped or disconnected hoses and confirm proper drainage during a water test.
symptoms: Water pooling on front passenger floorboard
Damp carpet or headliner after rain or car wash
Dripping or trickling sounds inside the cabin

before.title: Tow Hitch Harness Water Intrusion Causing Fire Risk (Recall 23V-181)
before.description: On 2022-2023 Santa Cruz vehicles equipped with a factory or dealer-accessory tow hitch harness, water can enter the harness module and collect on the printed circuit board, causing an electrical short. The short can cause the module to overheat or ignite, posing a fire risk while the vehicle is parked (even off) or being driven.
before.solution: Recall 23V-181 remedy: as an interim step dealers remove the tow-hitch fuse; the final repair installs a new fuse and a wire-extension kit free of charge. Owners were advised to park outside and away from structures until repaired. Confirm completion by VIN at nhtsa.gov.
symptoms: Burning smell from rear of vehicle
Smoke or thermal damage near trailer wiring module
Fire risk even when parked and off

citations.title: NHTSA Part 573 Safety Recall Report 23V-181
Recall 23V-181: Tow Hitch Harness Fire While Parked or Driving (Owner Forum)

proposal.title: Tow Hitch Harness Water Intrusion Causing Fire Risk (Recall 23V-181)
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 23V-181 (Hyundai recall 244) covers model-year 2022-2023 Santa Cruz vehicles that may have a Hyundai accessory tow-hitch harness. The harness module printed circuit board can be susceptible to water entering through the 4-pin tow-hitch harness connector. An electrical short can cause a trailer-harness-module fire while driving or while parked with the ignition off.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for NHTSA recall 23V-181 and park the vehicle outside and away from structures until the remedy is complete. Hyundai dealers verify whether the accessory tow hitch is installed and fit a 15-ampere fuse and new wire-extension kit as necessary, free of charge. The filing also describes fuse removal as interim protection until the final remedy is completed.
symptoms: No advance warning identified in the Part 573 report

before.title: Transmission Electric Oil Pump Fault Causing Loss of Drive Power (Recall 22V-746)
before.description: On 2022 Santa Cruz models with the 8-speed wet dual-clutch transmission, an internal fault in the electric oil pump (from insufficient soldering on its circuit board) can impair the transmission's fail-safe limited-mobility mode. Owners report a warning for 20-30 seconds followed by a complete loss of motive power and inability to accelerate. Loss of drive power is among the most-complained-about defects on the early Santa Cruz.
before.solution: Recall 22V-746 remedy: dealers inspect and replace the transmission as necessary and update the transmission control unit (TCU) software free of charge. Verify recall completion by VIN at nhtsa.gov.
symptoms: Sudden loss of motive power / inability to accelerate
Vehicle drops into limited-mobility or fail-safe mode
Warning lights for transmission / check engine
20-30 seconds of normal power then loss of drive

citations.title: 2022 Hyundai Santa Cruz Recalls (Cars.com / NHTSA)
2022 Hyundai Santa Cruz Problems & Complaints Guide

proposal.title: Transmission Electric Oil Pump Fault Causing Loss of Drive Power (Recall 22V-746)
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 22V-746 (Hyundai recall 236) covers certain model-year 2022 Santa Cruz vehicles. An internal fault in the transmission high-pressure electric oil pump can trigger diagnostic codes and warning lamps. Improper software logic for the fail-safe condition can allow about 20-30 seconds of motive power before the transmission clutches and drive gears disengage, causing a complete loss of motive power and increasing crash risk.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for NHTSA recall 22V-746. Hyundai dealers inspect the transmission and replace it if necessary, then reprogram the transmission control unit with software that provides proper fail-safe driving capability, free of charge.
symptoms: Complete loss of motive power after a brief limited-mobility period

before.title: Factory Bed Liner Peeling / Delaminating
before.description: The factory-applied composite bed liner on the Santa Cruz peels, chips, and delaminates prematurely, often within the first year. The issue begins at the edges and tailgate area. UV exposure and temperature cycling cause the liner adhesion to fail. This is a widespread cosmetic issue that affects bed usability.
before.solution: File a warranty claim for bed liner delamination - Hyundai has been replacing liners under warranty. For a permanent fix, owners recommend having the factory liner removed and replaced with a LINE-X or Rhino Liner spray-in bed liner ($450-650). The factory liner replacement is free under warranty but the issue may recur.

citations.title: Reddit r/HyundaiSantaCruz - Bed liner peeling already

communityRecommendations.content: LINE-X spray-in bed liner is the most popular upgrade replacing the factory liner
Remove the factory liner completely before applying aftermarket liner - applying over the factory liner causes adhesion issues

before.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing / Black Screen
before.description: The 10.25-inch infotainment system in the Santa Cruz is prone to freezing, going black, or rebooting randomly. Wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay connections can trigger the freezes. The backup camera feed may also be lost during a freeze. Hyundai has released multiple software updates to improve stability.
before.solution: Request the latest navigation/infotainment software update from the dealer (free). A hard reset can be performed by pressing and holding the power/volume knob for 10+ seconds. If issues persist, the head unit may need replacement ($1,000-2,000 at dealer). Switching from wireless to wired CarPlay/Android Auto reduces freezes.

citations.title: NHTSA Complaints - Santa Cruz Display

communityRecommendations.content: Use a wired connection for CarPlay/Android Auto instead of wireless - wireless triggers most of the freezing issues
Hard reset by holding the power knob for 10 seconds fixes most temporary freezes without needing a dealer visit
Professional OBD-II diagnostic scanner for reading infotainment and body module codes
OEM-quality replacement sensor for accurate readings and proper system function

before.title: Rear Window and Tailgate Rattle / Wind Noise
before.description: The rear sliding window and tailgate area of the Santa Cruz develops rattles and wind noise, particularly at highway speeds. The rear window weatherstripping and tailgate seal are inadequate, allowing air intrusion and vibration. Some owners also report water leaks around the rear window seal.
before.solution: Apply adhesive-backed foam weatherstripping tape to the rear window frame to reduce rattling. The dealer can adjust tailgate alignment and replace weatherstripping under warranty. Hyundai updated the rear window seal in later production (part 87160-K4000). DIY foam tape fix costs $10-20; dealer seal replacement is $100-300.
symptoms: Rattle from rear of cabin at highway speed

communityRecommendations.content: 3M adhesive-backed foam weatherstrip tape applied to the rear window frame eliminates the rattle for $10
Check if the rear window is fully closed by running your finger along the seal - a gap as small as 1mm causes significant rattle
